Single-cell foundation models · breast cancer · design committed before data (commit 8d2c2d0)

Foundation-model cell states predict breast-cancer survival no better than a linear baseline, in TCGA and in METABRIC

Natalija Stepurko · October 2026 · natalija-stepurko.com · code

Cell states were defined in 50,002 cells from 152 donors of a breast-cancer single-cell atlas with two single-cell foundation models, scGPT and Geneformer, and with a linear baseline, HVG-PCA: principal component analysis (PCA) of the highly variable genes (HVGs). Each state's marker genes were scored as a signature in 1,094 tumours of The Cancer Genome Atlas breast cohort (TCGA-BRCA; 151 deaths) and tested for overall survival (OS) against outcome permutations, random gene sets matched for size and expression, and clinical references: age, stage and the PAM50 (Prediction Analysis of Microarray, 50 genes) intrinsic subtype. In the pre-specified risk direction no representation's best signature cleared its family-wise permutation null (p = 0.16 HVG-PCA, 0.13 scGPT, 0.37 Geneformer), and each foundation model's margin over the baseline in concordance index (C-index) above the random-gene floor was negative (scGPT −0.021, Geneformer −0.039), measured against a baseline pick that is a single-dataset state with a low floor. Added to age and stage, no pick changed the cross-validated C-index by more than −0.002 to +0.001 under nested selection (only HVG-PCA's either-direction family maximum added, +0.007); the published 11-gene proliferation score of PAM50 added +0.008. With the signatures frozen before outcomes were read, all 8 foundation-model-minus-baseline margins were negative in 1,979 patients of the Molecular Taxonomy of Breast Cancer International Consortium (METABRIC); the interval lies below zero for one of the four pre-specified comparisons (Geneformer, OS) and for all four post hoc ones.

Key result

No representation beats chance selection in the pre-specified direction. The largest C-index in each representation's family of 201–369 signatures stays inside its family-wise null (p = 0.16 HVG-PCA, 0.13 scGPT, 0.37 Geneformer). Read in the direction each signature acts (post hoc), the family maxima of HVG-PCA (p = 0.024) and scGPT (p = 0.034) clear their nulls and Geneformer's (p = 0.052) does not (scGPT and Geneformer within two Monte-Carlo standard errors of 0.05). The margin-selected picks shown in the figures do not clear the null in either reading (p = 0.066, 0.098 and 0.17 either direction; 0.70, 0.13 and 0.59 pre-specified). No foundation-model pick is further above its random-gene floor than the baseline's pick; in the pre-specified reading the margins are −0.021 for scGPT (95% interval −0.078 to +0.012) and −0.039 for Geneformer (−0.084 to −0.001); Geneformer's interval lies below zero, with its upper bound −0.001 near zero. scGPT's pick has the higher C-index (0.576 against 0.547) and also the higher floor (0.502 against 0.453); the baseline pick it is measured against is the single-dataset state described below and does not itself beat chance (p = 0.70). Against the baseline's luminal sensitivity pick the margins are −0.010 and −0.013, with intervals spanning zero.

No pick adds to age and stage. Age and stage alone reach a cross-validated C-index of 0.751 (1,072 patients); the PAM50 subtype call alone reaches 0.525 (821 patients). With the signature re-selected inside every training fold, adding a pick changes the cross-validated C-index by −0.0016 to +0.0008, and every pick's change spans zero across the five repeats; the published 11-gene proliferation score adds +0.008. In this cohort PAM50 subtype adds nothing to age and stage either (0.732 against 0.733 on the 821 patients with a call), so the test has little room to show added value.

The replication in METABRIC points the same way. With signatures and directions frozen before its outcomes were read, every foundation-model-minus-baseline margin is negative (intervals below zero: 1 of 4 pre-specified, 4 of 4 post hoc). The published proliferation score replicates most strongly (OS C = 0.583 against a floor 95th percentile of 0.545; disease-specific survival (DSS) C = 0.637). Both HVG-PCA picks replicate. Of the foundation-model picks only Geneformer's risk pick meets the criterion, on DSS and by +0.0015 (borderline). Within luminal A tumours scGPT's protective pick has C = 0.562 (outcome-permutation p = 0.001; no random-gene floor, and not a pre-specified replication criterion); Geneformer's protective pick does not replicate.

What the cell states are

Each representation's pick is the state whose signature lies furthest above its own random-gene floor: in the risk direction for the pre-specified analysis, in either direction for the sensitivity analysis. Composition is from the 50,002-cell atlas; markers are ranked by a Wilcoxon test of the state against all other cells.

Composition: donors and datasets with, in brackets, the share of the state's cells from the largest one, then the most frequent annotated cell type and its share. A state is flagged single-donor when one donor supplies at least 80% of its cells. ER, PR: oestrogen and progesterone receptor; HER2: the ERBB2 gene product.

Most picks are tumour-cell programmes that follow the intrinsic subtypes. In the risk direction, scGPT's pick is an ERBB2-containing luminal epithelial programme and Geneformer's a basal keratin programme. In the protective direction, HVG-PCA and scGPT both recover a luminal, oestrogen-responsive programme (GATA3, XBP1, AZGP1, TRPS1 in both lists). Their marker lists contain genes of the subtype axes that carry most prognostic information in breast cancer (Wirapati et al. 2008), so their bulk scores are expected to track PAM50 subtype; that association was not measured here. Malignant cells cluster by patient in single-cell data (Tirosh et al. 2016): Geneformer's pre-specified pick (91% of its cells from one donor) and HVG-PCA's sensitivity pick (98%) are essentially one patient's tumour cells, and HVG-PCA's pre-specified pick (83%) is the single-dataset state below. Across all kept states, 50 of 123 HVG-PCA, 6 of 67 scGPT and 10 of 71 Geneformer states are single-donor: the foundation models group cells across patients more often than HVG-PCA without batch correction does, and this did not make their signatures more prognostic in bulk.

The baseline's pre-specified pick is a single-dataset artefact. Its cells are annotated as exhausted T cells, yet its markers are testis and colon genes (CEACAM7, TKTL1, FAM9C, INSL3), and none of the canonical T-cell markers (CD3D, CD3E, CD3G, CD2, CD4, CD8A, PTPRC) is among its 50 genes; it does include IKZF4, a regulatory-T-cell transcription factor, and the cell-cycle genes CDK2 and ERCC6L. It was picked because its random-gene floor is low (0.453), which makes its margin large although its C-index (0.547) is not. The pre-specified P2 margins are measured against it.

Geneformer's protective pick is a mixed-lineage state. Its markers are nuclear-retained transcripts and immediate-early genes, the profile of low-quality or dissociation-stressed cells.

Figure 2 places the picks in each representation's two-dimensional uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) of all 50,002 cells.

Does anything add to clinical information?

Each pick is added to a Cox proportional-hazards model of age and stage (1,072 patients, 142 deaths) and to age, stage and PAM50 subtype (821 patients, 116 deaths). The ladder's C-indices are of the score alone; this section asks whether the score adds to what a clinician already has.

The hazard ratios are nominal: every pick was chosen on the outcomes of these patients. The change in cross-validated C-index repeats the selection, and the choice of direction, inside every training fold, so it carries no selection. On that measure every pick's change in C spans zero across the five repeats. The luminal protective picks of HVG-PCA and scGPT keep nominal hazard ratios below 1 with PAM50 in the model (0.74 and 0.81 per standard deviation), but under nested selection they do not raise the cross-validated C-index. The published proliferation score (a fixed gene list, chosen after the first run to implement the design's published-signature rung, and pre-specified for METABRIC) is free of selection; it adds +0.008 to age and stage and nothing once PAM50 is in the model (−0.003). Of the family maxima, only HVG-PCA's either-direction maximum adds under nested selection (+0.007), and it too stops adding once PAM50 is in the model.

All of a representation's states at once

A ridge-penalised Cox model with every state of a representation (50-gene signatures: 123 HVG-PCA, 67 scGPT, 71 Geneformer) plus age and stage does not improve on age and stage alone (Figure 4); differences of a few thousandths are within the spread across fold seeds. Gradient-boosted survival models (XGBoost, Cox objective, fixed hyperparameters) fall below age and stage alone with every representation's states (0.703–0.730), so they are not read as a comparison between representations. Adding PAM50 subtype to age and stage does not raise the cross-validated C either.

Models within one section share their cross-validation folds; sections use different fold seeds, so the same model can differ by up to 0.009 between sections (age + stage 0.750–0.752; PAM50 + age + stage 0.723 and 0.732).

Independent replication in METABRIC

Specified in DESIGN §13 and committed (2ebb73e) before any frozen signature was scored against METABRIC outcomes; the results followed in 35c9233. The stage refuses to run on real outcomes unless the frozen file is committed and unmodified, and it was first run on permuted outcomes.

METABRIC (Curtis et al. 2012; Pereira et al. 2016) is an expression-microarray cohort with long follow-up: 1,979 patients, 1,143 deaths (OS). Disease-specific survival (DSS) is the secondary endpoint; it censors deaths from other causes, leaving 646 events. Twelve signatures were frozen with their genes and TCGA directions: the six picks, the family maxima and the proliferation reference. Nothing was re-selected or re-oriented. A signature replicates on an endpoint if its C, read in the TCGA direction, exceeds the 95th percentile of its METABRIC floor and its age-adjusted hazard ratio, stratified by METABRIC cohort, points in the TCGA direction with p < 0.05.

C is read in the direction fixed in TCGA. Floor p95: 95th percentile of 200 matched random gene sets in METABRIC. HR/SD: age-adjusted hazard ratio per standard deviation of the score in that direction, stratified by METABRIC cohort. Borderline: C within two approximate Monte-Carlo standard errors of the floor p95 (normal approximation from the floor mean and p95). Within-subtype p: 1,000 outcome permutations; 0.001 is the smallest value attainable.

Verdict. The replication shows no foundation-model advantage (figure 6). Geneformer's risk pick meets the criterion on DSS by +0.0015, within Monte-Carlo error of the floor p95. Within luminal A tumours scGPT's protective pick has C = 0.562 with outcome-permutation p = 0.001; no random-gene floor was computed within subtypes, so this is a result, not a pre-specified replication.

Random gene sets predict survival in METABRIC. With 1,143 deaths, the matched-random floors have 95th percentiles of 0.52–0.57. Some signatures have hazard-ratio p-values below 10−5 and still do not beat random genes: Geneformer's risk pick (OS), scGPT's risk pick (OS and DSS). This is the effect described by Venet et al. 2011.

The baseline's artefact pick replicates on both endpoints. Why it replicates was not examined in the tracked analysis; its 50 genes include the cell-cycle genes CDK2 and ERCC6L.

Approach

The three representations share everything except the representation itself: the cells, the clustering method, the marker ranking, the gene universe, the scoring and the survival statistics.

Assemble the atlas

CELLxGENE Census release 2025-11-08: every breast-carcinoma disease label, primary data only, droplet-based 3′ and 5′ chemistries. After quality control, 50,002 cells from 152 donors in 8 datasets were sampled in proportion to their 48 annotated cell types. No batch correction was applied; 63% of the cells come from one collection (Chen A et al. 2026). 577 cells (1.2%) duplicate another atlas cell exactly (identical raw counts, same donor), between that collection's Global Atlas and its compartment datasets; they were not removed (49,425 unique cells).

Represent every cell three ways

HVG-PCA: the 2,000 most variable genes, log-normalised, reduced to 50 principal components fitted on this atlas. scGPT (Cui et al. 2024): the whole-human checkpoint, pretrained on non-malignant human cells, cell embedding from its classification token. Geneformer (Theodoris et al. 2023): the 6-layer V1 model, pretrained on a corpus that excluded malignant cells, mean-pooled cell embedding. Both models run in bfloat16 on CPU; the model revisions in the configuration were pinned after the embedding run and match the only downloaded snapshot of each model.

Find cell states

Leiden clustering (Traag et al. 2019) of each representation's 15-nearest-neighbour graph at resolutions 0.3, 0.5, 1.0; states with at least 200 cells are kept: 123 HVG-PCA, 67 scGPT and 71 Geneformer states.

Turn states into signatures

The top 25, 50, 100 marker genes of each state (Wilcoxon test against all other cells), drawn only from the 16,297 genes also measured in the bulk cohort (1,526 of them highly variable): 369, 201 and 213 signatures.

Score the signatures in TCGA-BRCA

Each of 1,094 primary tumours (Cancer Genome Atlas Network 2012) gets one score per signature: the mean of the signature genes' expression, each z-scored across patients. The ladder uses Harrell's C (Harrell et al. 1982) of that score alone, without covariates. A Cox model with age and stage gives each pick's hazard ratio, reported separately (Figure 3).

Pick and read

Each representation's pick is the signature furthest above its own random-gene floor across all nine settings (three resolutions × three marker counts), chosen on TCGA outcomes. The family-wise null tests the family maximum, the largest C among a representation's signatures; read against the same null, the picks have p = 0.70, 0.13, 0.59 (pre-specified; HVG-PCA, scGPT, Geneformer) and 0.066, 0.098, 0.17 (either direction). A patient bootstrap that re-selects the pick in every resample gives the P2 margins. P1–P4 are then read off the ladder.

Controls

Every C-index sits on a ladder of controls, and findings are stated as distances between rungs.

nullSurvival outcomes permuted across patients 500 times. In each permutation the largest C-index among all of a representation's 201–369 signatures is kept, so the null includes the selection of a winner. The family-wise p of the observed maximum is read against it.
floor200 random gene sets per signature, matched for size and for mean-expression decile. In breast cancer most random gene sets are associated with outcome, largely through proliferation (Venet et al. 2011); the floor is what a gene list of that composition scores.
baselineThe HVG-PCA states, derived, scored and selected identically.
testThe scGPT and Geneformer states.
referencesAge + stage: cross-validated C 0.751 (1,072 patients; 0.732 on the 821 with a PAM50 call). PAM50 subtype alone (Parker et al. 2009): 0.525 cross-validated, 0.598 in sample. PAM50 + age + stage: 0.723. The published 11-gene proliferation score of PAM50 (Nielsen et al. 2010), chosen after the first run to fill the design's published-signature rung: C 0.569 against a floor mean of 0.480, permutation p = 0.0085 (10,000 permutations). Cross-validation is 5 × 5-fold, with this section's fold seed.

What the baseline controls for

All three representations are computed from the same expression matrix, and their signatures are scored on the same bulk genes. Prognostic signal present in all three can come from that shared input: cell-type composition, tumour purity or proliferation. The baseline measures what the shared input yields through a linear, unsupervised representation, and every claim about the foundation models is stated as the margin over it.

Predictions and how they came out

Four pass/fail predictions were committed to the repository with the analysis code on 2026-09-28 (8d2c2d0), before any data were downloaded; this is what "pre-specified" means on this page (there is no external registry). A review of the code against the design found that the first run computed some predictions differently from the text; both versions are kept in results/ladder/ladder.json, and the corrections draw from their own random streams, so no first-run number changed.

The design also wrote down, before the run, what each outcome would look like (DESIGN §7). The TCGA result matches none of the three shapes exactly. Test ≈ baseline, as in the second and third shapes. Every pick lies above its own random-gene floor, which the third shape ("both fail", test ≈ baseline ≈ floor) excludes, but no family clears its family-wise null, a rung the shapes do not name. On the reference, the data fit the second shape: every pick's C-index (0.546–0.591, in sample and selected on these outcomes) is far below age and stage (0.751, cross-validated). METABRIC, where every foundation-model margin is negative, points to the second.

Sensitivity analysis: direction of effect (post hoc)

Added on 2026-09-30, after the primary run (DESIGN §11). The pre-specified ladder is unchanged.

The design reads the C-index in one direction: a signature scores high only when a higher score means worse survival. Protective signatures turned out to be common and include the largest departures from 0.5 (C down to 0.400). The sensitivity analysis reads every signature in the direction it acts on the full cohort; its floor is read the same way, and the family-wise null takes the largest max(C, 1 − C) over the same 500 permutations. P3 is tested for every representation, the baseline included, with 10,000 within-subtype permutations; pick and direction were fixed on the full cohort, which contains these patients.

The signatures that clear the null are the family maxima; for HVG-PCA and scGPT these are different states from the picks carried into added value, replication and Figure 7. P2 still fails for both foundation models in this reading, and none of the pre-specified picks passes P3 (p = 0.38–0.40). Figure 7 shows the lead replicated signature as survival curves in TCGA, where it was selected: the HVG-PCA sensitivity pick, chosen by the rule in its caption.

Secondary endpoint: progression-free interval

The progression-free interval (PFI) was specified as the secondary endpoint for power, but in this cohort it has fewer events than OS (145 against 151). It runs through the same stages with the same statistics.

How the analysis runs

The pipeline is a Python package, scfm, whose stages are named commands. Each prints its plan with --dry-run before it touches data, so a person or a coding agent can inspect a run before starting it.

stagedoes
dataassemble the single-cell atlas and the bulk cohort; harmonise genes
embedone embedding per cell for HVG-PCA, scGPT, Geneformer
statesLeiden clusters per representation → marker-gene signatures
translatescore signatures in bulk; Cox; permutation null; matched-random floor; references
ladderassemble the ladder; patient bootstraps; test P1-P4, as coded and corrected
stratifycross-validated multivariable stratification: states vs age + stage
reportfigures, candidate shortlist, validation template
replicatefrozen signatures in METABRIC (run on its own; not part of 'all')
uv run scfm list                          # stages, interpreter, root and log path
uv run scfm run all --dry-run             # every stage's plan; dry runs are not logged
uv run scfm run translate -- --endpoint PFI
make reproduce && make verify             # tier A, then compare with results/MANIFEST.sha256

Run log and provenance

Every real run appends its command, start time, duration and exit code to results/run_log.json (47 runs so far). Every stage writes params.json beside its outputs: arguments, git commit and dirty flag, library versions and the pinned model revisions (scGPT a24c2377, Geneformer 1f7fbae4).

Checked downloads

Every file download (Xena, METABRIC) is checked against a sha256 before use; the atlas is pinned to Census release 2025-11-08 and the models to repository revisions. TCGA-BRCA from UCSC Xena (Goldman et al. 2020), survival from the TCGA Pan-Cancer Clinical Data Resource (Liu J et al. 2018):

  • HiSeqV2.gz 263bf67245cc…
  • BRCA_clinicalMatrix 39eb3be0fb86…
  • TCGA_CDR_survival.tsv a5e704158bb5…

METABRIC, cBioPortal datahub commit dca75cb3:

  • patient clinical table 2a6bbadc6e4b…
  • sample clinical table 9a2291e065e2…
  • expression matrix 4470069455a4…

Three reproduction tiers

A, from the tracked results (about 40 min, core environment): rebuilds translate, ladder, stratify and report for OS and PFI from the tracked signatures. B, from the embeddings: the per-cell embeddings are not distributed; with them, states onward reruns from the tracked cell list. C, from scratch (about 2 h 45 min on CPU, both environments): embedding took 1 h 44 min on 4 cores.

Tests, continuous integration and numerics

pytest covers the statistics, the stages' helpers and the Geneformer tokeniser, checked against the official tokeniser on a fixture; ruff lints. Continuous integration runs both on every pull request. A smoke run executes every stage except replicate, both foundation models included, on 2,000 cells. Embeddings are computed in bfloat16; scfm run embed -- --precision fp32 --limit 300 recomputes a subset in fp32, and no such comparison is tracked in results/.

Times are from results/run_log.json on a shared CPU machine. The atlas UMAP (figure 2) needs per-cell tables from states that are not tracked, so tier A does not rebuild it.

Deviations from the design and corrections

Where the first run computed something other than the design describes, or did not compute it. The full account, with every number, is DESIGN §12. The rows are read from results/ladder/ladder.json and results/stratify/cv_summary.json.

No pre-specified P1–P3 verdict changed. The corrections moved pre-specified P4 for scGPT and Geneformer from pass to not applicable; post hoc P1 for scGPT from fail to pass; post hoc P3 for scGPT and Geneformer from pass to fail; post hoc P4 for scGPT and Geneformer from pass to not applicable.

P1 statisticFamily-wise permutation null: the distribution of the best signature's C-index, so best-of-k is controlled at the ladder level.The signature with the largest above-floor margin was compared with the 95th percentile of the null of the family maximum.The family maximum (C; oriented C in the sensitivity analysis) with its family-wise p; P1 passes if the family-wise p < 0.05 and the maximising signature above its floor. The margin-selected pick's p against the same null is also given.
P2 marginTest against Baseline, both read as their distance above Floor; P2 passes if the bootstrap interval of the margin excludes zero.Raw C of the foundation-model pick minus raw C of the baseline pick, both picks held fixed in every bootstrap resample; floors not used.Above-floor margin (foundation-model pick minus baseline pick) with a patient bootstrap that re-selects each pick in every resample, floors held at full-cohort values; P2 passes if the lower 2.5% bound > 0.
P3 nullAt least one foundation-model-derived state is prognostic within a PAM50 subtype.Within-subtype C of the one margin-selected foundation-model signature above 0.6 in any subtype with at least 10 events; no null, not computed for the baseline.Max over subtypes (Basal, Her2, LumA, LumB) of the within-subtype C, against 10,000 within-subtype outcome permutations, for every representation including the baseline; P3 passes if p < 0.05. Pick and direction were fixed on the full cohort, which contains these patients.
Monte-Carlo errorDecisions at alpha = 0.05.Permutation p-values from 500 or 1,000 permutations, without Monte-Carlo error.Every permutation p carries its Monte-Carlo standard error (SE) and a borderline flag (within 2 SE of 0.05); P3 uses 10,000 permutations and the selection-aware P2 bootstrap 1,000 resamples (both their own streams). The family-wise null keeps its pre-specified 500 permutations.
P4 gatefoundation-model signatures that pass P2 are enriched for genes outside the HVG set.HVG fraction < 0.5 for the foundation-model pick, evaluated whether or not P2 passed; no enrichment test.Not applicable unless corrected P2 passes; when it does, a hypergeometric HVG-depletion test of the pick against the scored-gene universe and the pick's HVG fraction ranked among the baseline's signatures.
Ladder per settingCluster resolution and marker count are swept and the ladder is reported at each setting.One pick per representation across all nine settings, chosen by a survival-based margin.ladder_by_setting.csv: the pick at every (resolution, top-k), with the setting's family-wise p from its own sub-family null.
Covariate adjustmentCox models adjusted for age and stage in the primary model.Every ladder C-index is Harrell's C of the unadjusted score; the adjusted Cox model (lifelines penalizer 0.01, Wald p, per unit of the mean-z score) fed only the hr and p columns of scores.csv.added_value.csv: HR per SD, likelihood-ratio p and cross-validated change in C of each pick over age + stage (n with both) and over age + stage + PAM50, one row per role. Every pick and family maximum was selected, and its direction set, on the outcomes of the same patients; for those rows the likelihood-ratio p is not adjusted for selection and the fixed-signature CV change in C is optimistic. The nested CV columns redo the selection (and orientation) inside every training fold; only the published proliferation reference is free of selection. The lo/hi columns span fold repeats on the same patients, not a confidence interval.
Bootstrap intervalsBootstrap intervals over patients for the ladder.ladder.csv ci_lo/ci_hi and the as-coded P2 interval bootstrap the picked signatures with the pick held fixed, so they ignore the selection over 201-369 signatures per representation and are conditional on it; the as-coded P2 margin is the bootstrap mean of the raw C difference, not a full-cohort point estimate.Kept as coded; a separate field gives the full-cohort raw C difference, and the selection-aware P2 interval re-selects the picks in every resample.
Clustering stabilityCell-level clustering is done once; its stability is a separate diagnostic.The stability diagnostic was not run.Not run; the states are reported at three resolutions and nine settings instead (ladder_by_setting.csv).
Reference penaltyReference rung: PAM50 subtype.Cox reference fits use lifelines penalizer 0.01 (a ridge of 0.01 x n on standardised covariates).Each reference entry gives the penalizer, the in-sample C of the penalised fit and of the unpenalised fit (they differ for PAM50 alone, whose LumA and Basal hazards are nearly equal), and the cross-validated C, which is the figure to compare with.
Secondary endpointPFI is the secondary endpoint; both reported.Only OS was analysed.PFI run through translate and ladder into results/translate_pfi and results/ladder_pfi with the same statistics.
Stratification penaltyone lifelines ridge penalizer over all covariates, chosen by inner CVwith every covariate penalised, inner CV chose the smallest grid value in every fold, because larger values also shrank age and stage; the first run (all covariates penalised) gave ridge scGPT 0.7456 and ridge HVG-PCA 0.7525the ridge penalty applies to the state features only; age and stage keep 0.01

State labels. The first run labelled each state by its most frequent annotated cell type; the baseline's pre-specified pick was shown as an exhausted T-cell state. Donor, dataset and cell-type composition per state are now in results/states/state_composition.csv, and the page names programmes from marker genes.

Replication. METABRIC ran as specified in DESIGN §13. One patient with non-positive OS time is excluded, and one more from DSS with unknown status. Geneformer's protective pick is scored on 22 of its 25 genes (MALAT1, GAS5, SNHG6 have no probe), above the 80% minimum. METABRIC's subtype call is PAM50 plus claudin-low, taken as it is; stage is sparse there, so the Cox model adjusts for age and is stratified by METABRIC cohort.

Duplicate cells. 577 atlas cells (1.2%) have a raw count vector identical to another atlas cell from the same donor in a different dataset of the Chen et al. collection (343 between de5416ef and ed880090, 193 between 5a9cfb44 and de5416ef, 41 between 75011e96 and de5416ef): its Global Atlas repeats cells of its compartment datasets. The design did not foresee this, and the duplicates were not removed; the atlas holds 49,425 unique cells (results/report/atlas_duplicates.json, which also counts them per pick).

Model revisions. The tracked embeddings were computed before the model revisions were pinned in the configuration, and their params.json records no revision. The pinned revisions (scGPT a24c2377, Geneformer 1f7fbae4) are the only snapshots of each model in the download cache used for that run.

Limits

  • Neither model saw malignant cells in pretraining. The scGPT whole-human checkpoint was pretrained on non-diseased cells and Geneformer's corpus excluded malignant cells, while most of the picks here are malignant-cell states. Cancer-adapted checkpoints were not tested.
  • Light checkpoints. scGPT whole-human and the 6-layer Geneformer V1 model, run on CPU. A negative result is a result about these checkpoints.
  • One atlas, no batch correction. 8 datasets, 3′ and 5′ chemistries, pooled without integration; one baseline pick is confined to a single dataset.
  • Single-donor states. Three of the six picks, and 50, 6 and 10 of the HVG-PCA, scGPT and Geneformer states, draw at least 80% of their cells from one donor.
  • Duplicate cells. 577 cells (1.2%) duplicate other cells across Chen et al.'s Global Atlas and its compartment datasets; they were not removed.
  • Power. 151 deaths among 1,094 TCGA patients, with short follow-up; the TCGA Pan-Cancer Clinical Data Resource flags breast-cancer OS as needing longer follow-up (Liu J et al. 2018).
  • Selection in one cohort. The picks were chosen on TCGA outcomes. The family-wise null, the selection-aware bootstrap and the nested cross-validation pay for that choice within TCGA; METABRIC is the only out-of-sample test.
  • A bulk score is a proxy. The mean z-score of a state's markers mixes the state's abundance with tumour purity, proliferation and subtype.
  • One indication. Breast cancer was chosen for cohort size and established references; nothing here extends to other tumours until it is run there.

Related work

Carrying single-cell states into bulk cohorts to test prognosis is established: EcoTyper defined prognostic cell states and ecosystems across carcinomas (Luca et al. 2021); in breast cancer, Wu et al. 2021 deconvolved bulk cohorts into ecotypes with distinct outcomes, and Chen A et al. 2026, whose collection supplies 63% of this atlas's cells, found that the states whose associations held across cohorts were protective. Scissor (Sun et al. 2022) uses the bulk phenotype to choose cells, so its associations are not independent tests of outcome; here state discovery never sees outcomes. Random gene sets predict breast-cancer outcome, mostly through proliferation (Venet et al. 2011; Wirapati et al. 2008), which is the reason for the matched-random floor. Foundation models have been evaluated on cancer outcomes within single-cell cohorts (Roman et al. 2025) and on TCGA survival from bulk embeddings (Liu W et al. 2026), and simple baselines match them on zero-shot cell-level tasks (Kedzierska et al. 2025) and perturbation prediction (Ahlmann-Eltze et al. 2025; Bendidi et al. 2024). We found no prior study that combines foundation-model-defined states in a tumour atlas, a linear arm through the identical pipeline, matched-random and family-wise controls, predictions committed before the data, and a replication with frozen signatures. The related-work note in the repository (research/literature.md) covers the field and how each reference was verified.
